Owner agent: `quarkus-engineer-agent`  
Purpose: Complete cross-cutting controls without changing the approved no-auth posture.  
Requirements: SR-001..007; OR-006; NFR-005/006/011. Architecture: sections 13/17/19/20; ADR-001/003/005. DBML: Scheme privilege/readiness facts.  
Inputs: T018. Prohibited paths: auth libraries, external logging platform, audit store, sensitive labels.
Expected artifacts: liveness/readiness, structured safe telemetry, ArchUnit suite, blocking/context checks. Dependencies: Hard T018. Parallelizable: false where bootstrap/config overlaps; docs can follow independently.  
Instructions: Separate telemetry from audit; expose required rates/latencies/pools/cache/outbox/confirm/readiness reasons; prohibit sensitive values and enforce all architecture guardrails including no Scheme mutation/idempotency.  
Acceptance/verification: architecture/security telemetry tests pass; readiness/failure reasons are non-sensitive; liveness tolerates degradable dependencies.  
Risks/stop: stop on accidental auth/401/403, high-cardinality sensitive metric, logger dependency in core or missing mandatory readiness failure.

### T020 — Update implementation and operational documentation

Owner agent: `documentation-agent`  
Purpose: Align developer, API, security, migration, recovery and operations guidance with actual implementation.  
Requirements: OR-001..009; NFR-010; SR-002..007; CR-002..005. Architecture: sections 13-17. DBML: final mapping/read-only Scheme privileges.  
Inputs: T003/T010/T018/T019. Allowed paths: `README.md`, `docs/implementation/**`, `docs/operations/**`, `docs/security/**`, `docs/database/migration-guide.md`. Prohibited paths: approved requirements/architecture/DBML, source/tests/deployment.

Instructions: State no-auth residual risk, loopback-only requirement, no audit durability claim, no DB rollback, same-digest promotion and human merge control; never include secret values or production details.  
Acceptance/verification: links/commands/path references validate; docs match observed configuration/contracts.  
Risks/stop: stop if operational owner/recurrence/threshold is unknown—mark pending rather than invent.

### T021 — Validate architecture and LikeC4 mechanically

Owner agent: `test-implementation-agent`  
Purpose: Produce executable strict-boundary and LikeC4 validation evidence before quality gates.  
Requirements: NFR-005/007; AC-000. Architecture: model and guardrails; CAG-301. DBML: no change.  
Inputs: T019, approved architecture bytes. Allowed paths: `src/test/java/com/alexastudillo/partyregistry/architecture/**`, `docs/implementation/architecture-validation.md`; build path only through a separately scoped T005 repair if tooling is absent. Prohibited paths: architecture source semantic edits.
Expected artifacts: ArchUnit results and repository-controlled LikeC4 parse/validate/render procedure/results. Dependencies: Hard T019. Parallelizable: true with T020.  
Instructions: Verify no cycles/leaks, no Scheme administration/idempotency, reviewed model parses and required views render; syntax correction requires architecture authority, not this task.  
Acceptance/verification: executable checks pass with exact commands/exit codes and artifact digest; manual-only evidence is insufficient for final quality approval.  
Risks/stop: stop if tooling requires unapproved dependency/network installation or semantic model edit.

### T035 — Discover the approved restricted deployment interface

Owner agent: `infrastructure-discovery-agent`
Purpose: Identify the existing authorised VPS/Podman wrapper or deployment interface needed by T022/T034 without changing infrastructure or exposing credentials.
Requirements: OR-001..006; deployment profile prohibition on direct SSH/unrestricted shell and requirement for rootless Podman/Quadlet. Architecture: sections 16/21 AR-004. DBML: not applicable.
Inputs: approved deployment profile, repository deployment inventory, authorised environment metadata supplied by `factoryctl`. Allowed paths: none (read-only discovery). Prohibited paths: repository writes, remote mutation, unrestricted shell, credential/secret output, provisioning and deployment.

Dependencies: Hard T023 and authorised discovery-phase invocation. Parallelizable: true with independent read-only quality gates after frozen inputs.
Instructions: Verify rather than invent the restricted interface; distinguish observed facts from unavailable details; do not test by deploying.

### T022 — Prepare OCI and Quadlet deployment artifacts in later deployment phase

Owner agent: `deployment-engineer-agent`  
Purpose: Implement approved rootless, non-public runtime descriptors without deploying during implementation.  
Requirements: OR-001..006; NFR-008/010/011; AC-015/026. Architecture: section 16; deployment profile. DBML: forward-only startup/migration separation.

Expected artifacts: non-root OCI definition, health check, loopback port, rootless Quadlet, external config/secret references, limits/restart/logging/runbook. Dependencies: Hard T023/T035 and workflow entry to authorised deployment phase. Parallelizable: false with deployment execution.
Instructions: Preserve nginx/internal boundary, separate runtime/migration DB credentials, same digest promotion and rollback image retention; exact resource values must be approved/measured config.

24:

26: |---|---|
27: | `createParty` | FR-001/002/007/008/010/011/015/016; AC-001/002/011/012/019/023/030/036 |

Details have retrieval and conditional update but no independent deletion or lifecycle operation. Archive, revoke, and nationality end are explicit logical lifecycle operations; no HTTP DELETE implies physical deletion.
42: 
43: ## Context, concurrency, error, and cache contract
44: 
45: - Every business operation accepts mandatory `tenant-id` (canonical lowercase UUID) and `user-id` (1..128), plus optional canonical lowercase UUID `process-id`. The service generates a process ID when absent and returns the effective value in the `process-id` response header. No tenant field exists in a body.
46: - V1 has no OpenAPI security scheme. No operation defines HTTP 401 or 403.
47: - Modifications of existing aggregates require `If-Match: "<non-negative-version>"`. Absence is HTTP 428 / `PRECONDITION_REQUIRED`; mismatch is HTTP 412 / `VERSION_CONFLICT`. Successful versioned results expose `ETag` and do not duplicate version in response bodies.
48: - Errors use the `ApiResponse` shape (`status`, `code`, `data`) and the effective categories `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `PRECONDITION_REQUIRED`, `VERSION_CONFLICT`, `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`, and `INTERNAL_ERROR`. `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` is absent. Error data cannot carry stack traces, SQL/provider internals, or complete identifiers.
49: - Cross-tenant lookup is indistinguishable from absence and returns the standard 404 envelope.
50: - The decryption operation alone returns plaintext. Its success and failure responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`; successful disclosure occurs only after local structured security-log emission.
51: 
52: ## TC-001 query decision
53: 
54: The reversible parameter spelling and serialization are:
55: 
56: - `page`: one decimal integer, zero-based, default `0`.
57: - `size`: one decimal integer, default `20`, inclusive range `1..100`.
58: - Party filters: optional single-value `type` and `status`.
59: - Nationality filters within path-scoped Party: optional single-value `countryCode`, `primary`, and `active`.
60: - Party Identifier filters: optional single-value `partyId`, `identifierSchemeId`, `status`, and `primary`.
61: - Party/Scheme lookup selection: optional `selection=ALL|VERIFIED_PRIMARY`, default `ALL`.
62: - V1 exposes no client-selectable `sort` parameter. Every paginated result is ordered by resource UUID ascending, which is therefore both the sole order and deterministic tie-breaker.
63: - Repeated parameters, comma-separated lists, empty values, unknown parameters/filters, unsupported selection values, negative pages, and out-of-range sizes are `VALIDATION_ERROR`. Parameter names are case-sensitive; enum and country-code values use their documented uppercase representation.
64: 
65: These spellings implement only TC-001's delegated technical authority; they do not add search scope. Amendment 002 removes Identifier Scheme browse/search parameters and endpoints.
66: 
67: ## Event catalog, publication, and compatibility
68: 
69: The immutable schema catalog contains exactly:
70: 
71: - `party.created.v1`, `party.updated.v1`, `party.activated.v1`, `party.inactivated.v1`, `party.archived.v1`;
72: - `party.nationality-added.v1`, `party.nationality-updated.v1`, `party.nationality-removed.v1`;
73: - `party.identifier-created.v1`, `party.identifier-updated.v1`, `party.identifier-verified.v1`, `party.identifier-rejected.v1`, `party.identifier-expired.v1`, `party.identifier-revoked.v1`.
74: 
75: Every event carries stable `eventId`, versioned `eventType`, `schemaVersion=1`, `tenantId`, aggregate identity/type/version, occurrence time, optional correlation/causation, and a minimal typed payload. Identifier payloads contain only IDs and lifecycle state; they contain no plaintext, ciphertext, HMAC fingerprint, mask, issuer, verification actor, or confidential Party attributes. Examples are synthetic.
76: 
77: Messages are persistent, published to the approved durable topic exchange with publisher confirms, and delivered at least once. Retries/recovery retain the same event ID. Consumers own queues/DLQs and deduplicate by event ID. Published V1 schema meanings are immutable; an incompatible change requires a newly approved versioned event type/schema rather than mutation of V1.
78: 
79: ## Compatibility and explicit exclusion inventory
80: 
81: The following are intentionally absent and must remain absent from generated interfaces and runtime adapters:
82: 
83: 1. Identifier Scheme lookup, browse, search, create, update, status, retire, delete, background mutation, or Scheme event contracts.
84: 2. Public outbox read/write/status/retry/recovery administration. Authorized failed-event recovery is an internal operational boundary, not REST.
85: 3. `Idempotency-Key`, command replay, request fingerprints, replay stores, and `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.
86: 4. Authentication/security schemes, login, roles, permissions, Keycloak/Access Management request integration, and HTTP 401/403.
87: 5. Plaintext in ordinary responses, listings, events, telemetry, error messages, examples, or persistence contracts.
88: 6. Ciphertext, fingerprints, key material, stack traces, SQL details, provider bodies, tenant identifiers in request bodies, physical database names, and persistence entities.
89: 7. HTTP DELETE operations for business records, physical deletion, automatic purge, Party-detail deletion/lifecycle, and clock-driven lifecycle transitions.
90: 8. Scheme, database, Flyway, platform, infrastructure, audit-store, or decryption events.
91: 
92: No breaking V1 REST or event meaning is authorized. Additive changes still require requirements traceability and independent API-contract review; incompatible changes require a separately approved contract version.
93:

101: 
102: The T036 harness reported: `Validated OpenAPI document, JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 catalog, and 2 event example(s).` No contract defect was demonstrated, so the existing versioned OpenAPI document, event schema, and examples were preserved unchanged.

- Repeated parameters, comma-separated lists, empty values, unknown parameters/filters, unsupported selection values, negative pages, and out-of-range sizes are `VALIDATION_ERROR`. Parameter names are case-sensitive; enum and country-code values use their documented uppercase representation.

These spellings implement only TC-001's delegated technical authority; they do not add search scope. Amendment 002 removes Identifier Scheme browse/search parameters and endpoints.

## Event catalog, publication, and compatibility

The immutable schema catalog contains exactly:

- `party.created.v1`, `party.updated.v1`, `party.activated.v1`, `party.inactivated.v1`, `party.archived.v1`;
- `party.nationality-added.v1`, `party.nationality-updated.v1`, `party.nationality-removed.v1`;
- `party.identifier-created.v1`, `party.identifier-updated.v1`, `party.identifier-verified.v1`, `party.identifier-rejected.v1`, `party.identifier-expired.v1`, `party.identifier-revoked.v1`.

Every event carries stable `eventId`, versioned `eventType`, `schemaVersion=1`, `tenantId`, aggregate identity/type/version, occurrence time, optional correlation/causation, and a minimal typed payload. Identifier payloads contain only IDs and lifecycle state; they contain no plaintext, ciphertext, HMAC fingerprint, mask, issuer, verification actor, or confidential Party attributes. Examples are synthetic.

Messages are persistent, published to the approved durable topic exchange with publisher confirms, and delivered at least once. Retries/recovery retain the same event ID. Consumers own queues/DLQs and deduplicate by event ID. Published V1 schema meanings are immutable; an incompatible change requires a newly approved versioned event type/schema rather than mutation of V1.

## Compatibility and explicit exclusion inventory

The following are intentionally absent and must remain absent from generated interfaces and runtime adapters:

1. Identifier Scheme lookup, browse, search, create, update, status, retire, delete, background mutation, or Scheme event contracts.
2. Public outbox read/write/status/retry/recovery administration. Authorized failed-event recovery is an internal operational boundary, not REST.
3. `Idempotency-Key`, command replay, request fingerprints, replay stores, and `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.
4. Authentication/security schemes, login, roles, permissions, Keycloak/Access Management request integration, and HTTP 401/403.
5. Plaintext in ordinary responses, listings, events, telemetry, error messages, examples, or persistence contracts.
6. Ciphertext, fingerprints, key material, stack traces, SQL details, provider bodies, tenant identifiers in request bodies, physical database names, and persistence entities.
7. HTTP DELETE operations for business records, physical deletion, automatic purge, Party-detail deletion/lifecycle, and clock-driven lifecycle transitions.
8. Scheme, database, Flyway, platform, infrastructure, audit-store, or decryption events.

No breaking V1 REST or event meaning is authorized. Additive changes still require requirements traceability and independent API-contract review; incompatible changes require a separately approved contract version.

## T036 validation evidence

Executed for T003 on 2026-08-15:

| Command | Exit | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| `./gradlew --offline validateContracts` | `0` | Parsed `api/openapi/v1/party-registry.openapi.yaml` as OpenAPI 3.1 with references resolved, compiled `api/events/v1/party-registry-events.schema.json` as JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, discovered both files under `api/events/v1/examples/*.json`, and validated both examples against the catalog. |

The T036 harness reported: `Validated OpenAPI document, JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 catalog, and 2 event example(s).` No contract defect was demonstrated, so the existing versioned OpenAPI document, event schema, and examples were preserved unchanged.

156: ## 9. Contract, Domain, Application, Data, and Adapter Plan
157: 
158: ### Contract-first
159: 
160: T036 first adds the minimum repository-controlled OpenAPI 3.1 and JSON Schema 2020-12 validation harness needed by T003, including reference resolution and example validation. This is a build-time verification capability only: it introduces no runtime dependency or contract meaning, and its dependency choice remains subject to the independent supply-chain gate. T003 then applies TC-001 and defines every approved operation, context header, request/response, mask, no-store response, ETag/If-Match behavior, validation/error category, tenant non-disclosure rule, payload bound, and examples containing synthetic data only. It must exclude Scheme/outbox administration and idempotency. Versioned event schemas must cover only the approved Party/Identifier catalog, stable event identity, tenant/aggregate/version/correlation data, minimum payload, and no plaintext. T003 must execute the T036 harness over the OpenAPI document, all resolved references, the event schema, and every event example. T004 writes failing behavioral contract tests before T017.
161: 
162: **TECHNICAL CONTRACT DECISION TC-001.** Acting under the bounded authority explicitly delegated by requirements-gate PASS finding RG-401, V1 uses zero-based `page` with default `0`, `size` with default `20` and inclusive range `1..100`, and ascending resource UUID as the sole V1 order (and deterministic tie-breaker). Effective supported filter semantics are Party type/status, nationality country/primary/active within one Party, and Party Identifier Party/Scheme/status/primary; Amendment 002 removes all Identifier Scheme browse/search parameters with that endpoint. Negative pages, out-of-range sizes, unsupported filters, and unsupported sort fields/directions produce `VALIDATION_ERROR`. T003 may choose non-normative query-parameter spelling and serialization consistent with these semantics as a reversible technical contract decision, and T027 must independently validate it. TC-001 adopts downstream-resolvable technical values; it does not present RG-208 as original product authority.
163: 
164: ### Domain and application
165: 
166: T005/T006 cover Party type/detail, dates, nationalities, exact lifecycle matrices, immutability, masking, display-name normalization, identifier compatibility and errors. Domain receives no Quarkus/Jakarta/Mutiny/transport/persistence/logging/configuration imports. T007/T008 define input/output ports and use cases for Party/detail/nationality/Identifier only, pre-resolve geography before transaction, enforce tenant/context and If-Match, orchestrate protection, atomically request mutation/outbox, and order decrypt-log-before-return. No Scheme mutation or command-idempotency port is permitted.
167: 
168: ### Migration and persistence
169: 
170: T010 maps all 8 enums, 7 tables, five references, checks, named indexes, partial indexes, deferred detail triggers/function, UUIDv7 requirement, comments/defaults, runtime/migration privilege separation, and outbox semantics from DBML. It must not invent the final Flyway version until current migration inventory is rechecked. It validates a clean database, previous supported schema upgrade when one exists, representative data, locks/downtime, and failure recovery. Existing applied migrations are immutable and rollback is roll-forward only.
171: 
172: T011 keeps its completed database-first scope: migration inventory, PostgreSQL constraints, privileges, transaction/concurrency semantics, error-mapping fixtures, and an implementation-presence check. The current implementation result supplies material repository evidence that T009's application boundary cannot carry all approved persistence facts. T038 therefore adds failing application tests and an explicit OpenAPI/DBML-to-application-field map before T039 repairs only the affected boundary-neutral commands, intents, views, use cases and port-facing data flow. T039 must carry nationality `primary`; identifier creation `issuerCode`, `primary`, `issuedOn` and `expiresOn`; transition `verifiedAt`, `verifiedBy` and applicable `expiresOn`; and the persisted status/primary/issuer/lifecycle/verification/audit facts required by the approved query representation, without leaking transport or persistence models. T011 is then rerun to prove no database regression and to retain its expected adapter-presence failure before T012.
173: 
174: T012 implements the six persistence ports and must publish a bounded construction/test-fixture contract inside its assigned adapter documentation so a later independent test owner can instantiate the concrete adapter without guessing implementation details. T037 then verifies every port against PostgreSQL after T012. This sequencing is a bounded DAG repair: T038/T039 restore the missing application contract before adapter work, database behavior remains test-first, and concrete black-box adapter verification follows only because the concrete construction boundary does not exist beforehand. T012/T037 keep persistence models separate from domain, use reactive PostgreSQL and reactive transactions, tenant-qualify operations, bound pages/batches, map named constraints/SQLSTATE safely, increment aggregate versions atomically, expose a query-only Scheme catalog, and never hold transactions across remote I/O.
175: 
176: ### Integrations, security, observability, resilience
177: 
178: - Geographic calls use bounded reactive timeout, 24-hour cache, at-most-seven-day stale fallback, cold-cache 503, active-code mapping, and no transaction overlap.
179: - Protection uses separate runtime-injected encryption/HMAC masters, tenant derivation, authenticated encryption, exact uppercase HMAC representation, version handling, minimal plaintext lifetime, and no fallback secret.
180: - Local decryption logging emits required structured fields before disclosure, reports synchronous failure, and never claims remote durability.
181: - RabbitMQ uses persistent versioned messages, publisher confirms, bounded claim/publish/outcome phases, `SKIP LOCKED`, optimistic claim token, same event ID, no DLQ/discard/purge, and authorised internal failed-event recovery without public CRUD.
182: - Logs/metrics/traces omit plaintext, ciphertext, fingerprints, keys and confidential payloads. Health separates liveness, mandatory readiness, and degradable dependencies.

## 9. Contract, Domain, Application, Data, and Adapter Plan

### Contract-first

T036 first adds the minimum repository-controlled OpenAPI 3.1 and JSON Schema 2020-12 validation harness needed by T003, including reference resolution and example validation. This is a build-time verification capability only: it introduces no runtime dependency or contract meaning, and its dependency choice remains subject to the independent supply-chain gate. T003 then applies TC-001 and defines every approved operation, context header, request/response, mask, no-store response, ETag/If-Match behavior, validation/error category, tenant non-disclosure rule, payload bound, and examples containing synthetic data only. It must exclude Scheme/outbox administration and idempotency. Versioned event schemas must cover only the approved Party/Identifier catalog, stable event identity, tenant/aggregate/version/correlation data, minimum payload, and no plaintext. T003 must execute the T036 harness over the OpenAPI document, all resolved references, the event schema, and every event example. T004 writes failing behavioral contract tests before T017.

**TECHNICAL CONTRACT DECISION TC-001.** Acting under the bounded authority explicitly delegated by requirements-gate PASS finding RG-401, V1 uses zero-based `page` with default `0`, `size` with default `20` and inclusive range `1..100`, and ascending resource UUID as the sole V1 order (and deterministic tie-breaker). Effective supported filter semantics are Party type/status, nationality country/primary/active within one Party, and Party Identifier Party/Scheme/status/primary; Amendment 002 removes all Identifier Scheme browse/search parameters with that endpoint. Negative pages, out-of-range sizes, unsupported filters, and unsupported sort fields/directions produce `VALIDATION_ERROR`. T003 may choose non-normative query-parameter spelling and serialization consistent with these semantics as a reversible technical contract decision, and T027 must independently validate it. TC-001 adopts downstream-resolvable technical values; it does not present RG-208 as original product authority.

### Domain and application

T005/T006 cover Party type/detail, dates, nationalities, exact lifecycle matrices, immutability, masking, display-name normalization, identifier compatibility and errors. Domain receives no Quarkus/Jakarta/Mutiny/transport/persistence/logging/configuration imports. T007/T008 define input/output ports and use cases for Party/detail/nationality/Identifier only, pre-resolve geography before transaction, enforce tenant/context and If-Match, orchestrate protection, atomically request mutation/outbox, and order decrypt-log-before-return. No Scheme mutation or command-idempotency port is permitted.

### Migration and persistence

T010 maps all 8 enums, 7 tables, five references, checks, named indexes, partial indexes, deferred detail triggers/function, UUIDv7 requirement, comments/defaults, runtime/migration privilege separation, and outbox semantics from DBML. It must not invent the final Flyway version until current migration inventory is rechecked. It validates a clean database, previous supported schema upgrade when one exists, representative data, locks/downtime, and failure recovery. Existing applied migrations are immutable and rollback is roll-forward only.

T011 keeps its completed database-first scope: migration inventory, PostgreSQL constraints, privileges, transaction/concurrency semantics, error-mapping fixtures, and an implementation-presence check. The current implementation result supplies material repository evidence that T009's application boundary cannot carry all approved persistence facts. T038 therefore adds failing application tests and an explicit OpenAPI/DBML-to-application-field map before T039 repairs only the affected boundary-neutral commands, intents, views, use cases and port-facing data flow. T039 must carry nationality `primary`; identifier creation `issuerCode`, `primary`, `issuedOn` and `expiresOn`; transition `verifiedAt`, `verifiedBy` and applicable `expiresOn`; and the persisted status/primary/issuer/lifecycle/verification/audit facts required by the approved query representation, without leaking transport or persistence models. T011 is then rerun to prove no database regression and to retain its expected adapter-presence failure before T012.

T012 implements the six persistence ports and must publish a bounded construction/test-fixture contract inside its assigned adapter documentation so a later independent test owner can instantiate the concrete adapter without guessing implementation details. T037 then verifies every port against PostgreSQL after T012. This sequencing is a bounded DAG repair: T038/T039 restore the missing application contract before adapter work, database behavior remains test-first, and concrete black-box adapter verification follows only because the concrete construction boundary does not exist beforehand. T012/T037 keep persistence models separate from domain, use reactive PostgreSQL and reactive transactions, tenant-qualify operations, bound pages/batches, map named constraints/SQLSTATE safely, increment aggregate versions atomically, expose a query-only Scheme catalog, and never hold transactions across remote I/O.

### Integrations, security, observability, resilience

- Geographic calls use bounded reactive timeout, 24-hour cache, at-most-seven-day stale fallback, cold-cache 503, active-code mapping, and no transaction overlap.
- Protection uses separate runtime-injected encryption/HMAC masters, tenant derivation, authenticated encryption, exact uppercase HMAC representation, version handling, minimal plaintext lifetime, and no fallback secret.
- Local decryption logging emits required structured fields before disclosure, reports synchronous failure, and never claims remote durability.
- RabbitMQ uses persistent versioned messages, publisher confirms, bounded claim/publish/outcome phases, `SKIP LOCKED`, optimistic claim token, same event ID, no DLQ/discard/purge, and authorised internal failed-event recovery without public CRUD.
- Logs/metrics/traces omit plaintext, ciphertext, fingerprints, keys and confidential payloads. Health separates liveness, mandatory readiness, and degradable dependencies.

## 10. Testing Strategy and Architecture Enforcement

Tests precede or accompany production tasks as defined in `tasks.md`, except for the explicitly bounded T037 concrete-adapter suite: T038 adds the missing application contract tests before T039, T011 defines PostgreSQL behavior before T012, and T037 follows T012 only because the current approved sources expose no concrete adapter factory or constructor to target. T036 provides schema-validator self-tests before T003 relies on the harness. Required layers are pure domain tests, application tests with port fakes, OpenAPI/event contract tests, reactive API tests, PostgreSQL migration tests, post-construction persistence-port tests, provider integration tests, concurrency/fault/restart tests, security/redaction tests, architecture tests, pilot load/lag tests, packaged-runtime smoke tests, and deployment/recovery checks. T011 and T037 must execute where the pinned PostgreSQL 18 Testcontainers image can start; socket denial is an execution-environment blocker, not permission to skip or weaken either suite.

ArchUnit must mechanically prohibit framework imports in domain, concrete adapters in application, REST-to-persistence access, persistence model exposure, direct repository injection into use cases, Scheme mutation capability, package cycles, and unapproved dependencies. LikeC4 parse/validate/render remains a mandatory independent quality-gate check; it was previously `NOT_RUN` because repository-controlled tooling was absent. T021 may add the minimum justified validation mechanism only through the governed build task; it must not alter reviewed architecture semantics.

No test may use production data, real identifiers, secrets, trivial assertions, disabled checks, or implementation-exact mocks. Implementers may not delete or weaken tests to pass.

## 11. Phases, Dependency Graph, Waves, and Checkpoints

### Phases and critical path

1. Governance: TC-001/T001 -> T002.
2. Contract/foundation: T036 -> T003 -> T004.
3. Test-first core: T005 -> T006 -> T007 -> T008 -> T009; repair T038 -> T039.
4. Data: T010 + T039 -> T011 revalidation -> T012 -> T037.
5. Integrations/API: T013 -> T014; T015 + T037 -> T016; T017 and completed outbound adapters -> T018.
6. Cross-cutting/docs: T019 -> T020/T021.
7. Validation and release preparation: T023 -> T024..T029/T032; after T023 and T035, T022 -> T034; then immutable build T033 and readiness T030.
8. GitHub handoff: T031.

Critical path is TC-001 -> contract-validation harness -> validated contracts -> application ports -> persistence/integrations -> inbound API -> integration validation -> independent gates -> immutable candidate/readiness -> PR handoff.

### Parallel waves

| Wave | Tasks safe to run after dependencies | Checkpoint |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | T001 | TC-001 is recorded in this proposed plan as a delegated technical-contract decision; approved source files remain unchanged. |
| 1 | T002, then T036 | Issue/branch intent exists and the repository can validate OpenAPI 3.1, JSON Schema 2020-12, references, and examples without changing contract meaning. |
| 2 | T003, then T004; T005 after validated contract placement | Public/event contracts apply TC-001 and pass structural validation; failing behavioral contract tests express approved behavior. |
| 3 | T006 -> T007 -> T008 -> T009; T010 may run in parallel after T005 | Pure core/application and DB migration independently match approved sources. |
| 4 | T038; T013/T015/T017 may proceed in parallel because their paths do not overlap | Failing application tests and a field-flow map expose every approved value dropped by T009 without changing production code. |
| 5 | T039, then T011 revalidation; independent adapter-test tasks remain parallel where scopes do not overlap | Repaired application contracts carry all approved nationality/identifier facts, application tests pass, and PostgreSQL evidence remains green apart from the expected absent-adapter presence check. |
| 6 | T012, then T037; T014 may proceed in parallel after T012; T016 follows T037; T018 follows its adapter prerequisites | The concrete PostgreSQL adapter exposes a bounded construction contract, all six persistence ports receive black-box behavioral verification, and adapters satisfy stable ports/contracts without transaction or boundary leakage. |
| 7 | T019, T020, T021 | Cross-cutting evidence and documentation are aligned; full integration validation may begin. |
| 8 | T023, then independent T024-T029/T032; T035 -> T022 -> T034 may proceed in authorised later phases alongside frozen-input gates | Full validation and compliant deployment/release artifacts exist; direct SSH/cross-service references are absent. |
| 9 | T033, then T030 | One immutable candidate is identified and readiness-reviewed with all mandatory gates and deployment evidence. |
| 10 | T031 | PR handoff contains issue, scope, evidence, risks, rollout and rollback; no merge occurs. |

Shared bottlenecks are `build.gradle.kts`, `application.properties`, OpenAPI, migration ordering, and bootstrap wiring. Tasks touching those files are non-parallel or must be serialized by `factoryctl`.

## 12. Quality Gates and Evidence Package

| Gate | Trigger/input | Pass evidence | Repair owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code-quality-gate-agent` | All implementation | Clean build/static analysis, architecture boundaries, changed-file inventory | Responsible implementation agent |
| `test-quality-gate-agent` | Tests/behavior | Requirement-to-test coverage and non-trivial passing suites | `test-implementation-agent` |
| `security-gate-agent` | Releasable change | Tenant isolation, no-auth boundary, secret/plaintext/redaction/no-store/DB privilege evidence | Quarkus/test/deployment owner by finding |
| `dependency-supply-chain-gate-agent` | Build/dependencies, including T036 build-time validators | BOM alignment, validator minimality, runtime-classpath exclusion, vulnerability/license/secret scan, SBOM, reproducibility | Quarkus or build/release |
| `api-contract-gate-agent` | OpenAPI/events | TC-001, operation inventory, compatibility, examples and contract tests | Contract author |
| `database-migration-gate-agent` | Flyway/persistence | DBML mapping, clean/upgrade/representative tests, privileges, immutability | Database migration agent |
| `performance-reliability-gate-agent` | NFR-001..011 | Load/lag/startup/fault/recovery results under approved pilot profile | Test/integration owner |
| `production-readiness-gate-agent` | Candidate release | Same digest, rootless/loopback, health/smoke/stabilization, backup/restore/runbook | Build/deployment/docs owners |

`multiplatform-compatibility-gate-agent` is N/A: no Flutter or multiplatform behavior is in scope.

Completion evidence must be reproducible and include source commit, issue/branch/PR references when later created, changed-file inventory, exact build and test commands/exit codes, unit/contract/integration/migration/architecture/security/performance results, dependency and secret scans, SBOM, DBML-to-migration mapping, log/event redaction inspection, backup/restore and rollback/reconciliation evidence, OCI identifier/digest, environment promotion records, health/smoke/stabilization results, docs, and every gate result. Planned checks must never be represented as passed.

## 13. Traceability Matrix

| Obligation group | Implementation tasks | Verification tasks | Gates/evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC-000; NFR-004..007; DR-008/009; CR-005 | T036, T004, T010, T021, T022 | T036, T021, T023, T024 | Code, dependency, migration, production-readiness; schema-validation/build/profile/LikeC4 evidence |
| FR-001..003, 007, 010..012, 015..017, 021..033; VR-001/002/006/009..012; DR-001..003/005/007 | T006, T008, T039, T012, T014, T018 | T005, T007, T038, T011, T013, T017, T023 | Test, security, API, performance; AC-001..005, 011/012, 019/020, 023/024, 027, 030..043, 059/060, 067..070 |
| Amendment 001; FR-005/006/013/014/018/034..039/046..049; VR-003..005/007/008/013/014; DR-004; SR-001..007; CR-003 | T006, T008, T039, T012, T014, T018, T019 | T005, T007, T038, T011, T013, T017, T023, T037 | Security, API, migration, test; AC-007..010, 017, 021/022, 028, 044..050, 061/062, 071..079 |
| Amendment 002; effective FR-019/040..045/048/049; IR-004 | T008, T010, T012, T018 | T007, T011, T017, T021, T023/T024, T037 | Architecture/API/security/migration evidence proving query-only catalog and no Scheme API/event |
| FR-008/009/020/050; VR-015..018; DR-006; IR-002..004; NFR-001..003/009; CR-002/004 | T003, T008, T010, T016 | T004, T007, T011, T015, T023 | API, migration, reliability, security; AC-012..014, 016, 025, 029, 058, 063..066, 080 |

| Every DBML enum/table/reference/check/index/trigger/grant obligation and every persistence output port | T010, T039, T012 | T038, T011, T037, T024 | Application field-flow map, database migration gate, DBML mapping artifact, and black-box adapter evidence |

## 14. Complexity, Risks, and Decisions

### Deliberate complexity

| Item | Why required / simpler alternative | Risks / ownership / review condition |
|---|---|---|
| Transactional outbox | Required atomic event intent; direct publish is inconsistent | ADR-002; Quarkus/database owners; review only via new approved ADR |
| Authenticated encryption plus tenant HMAC | Restricted plaintext and exact protected lookup; plaintext/hash alternative is prohibited | ADR-003/004; security owner; rotation evidence required |
| Bounded Geographic cache | Approved availability semantics; direct-only calls fail BR-019 | Quarkus integration owner; no durable/distributed cache |
| Deferred Party/detail triggers and partial indexes | Explicit DBML invariants; application-only enforcement is concurrency-unsafe | Database migration owner; migration gate |
| Build-time OpenAPI 3.1 and JSON Schema 2020-12 validators | T003 cannot prove parsing, reference resolution, schema validity, or example conformance without executable tooling; manual inspection is insufficient | Quarkus build owner; dependencies must be minimal, absent from runtime classpaths, independently supply-chain reviewed, and removable only if an equivalent repository-controlled validator replaces them |

No new runtime container, broker, cache service, module, external logger, KMS, or privileged capability is planned.

### Risk register

| ID | Risk / trigger / impact | Mitigation and verification | Authority / stop condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-001 MEDIUM | Contract implementation drifts from delegated TC-001 or accidentally restores removed Scheme search | Contract/exclusion tests and independent API gate | Contract author/API gate; stop on semantic drift |
| R-002 HIGH | Approved unauthenticated internal decryption is exposed beyond loopback/internal nginx | Security and deployment negative tests; no public binding; no invented auth | Security/operations gates; stop on public exposure |
| R-003 HIGH | Plaintext, fingerprint, ciphertext or key reaches telemetry/event/repository | Model separation, redaction inspection, secret scans, fail closed | Security gate; stop on any exposure |
| R-004 HIGH | Migration diverges from DBML or risks destructive/irreversible data change | Exact mapping, representative upgrade, lock analysis, roll-forward recovery | Database gate/human DB authority; stop on conflict/destructive remediation |
| R-005 HIGH | Tenant predicate or Scheme runtime privilege is missing | Typed tenant ports, negative tests, SELECT-only privilege test | Security/database gates; stop on cross-tenant or catalog-write ability |
| R-006 MEDIUM | Outbox unknown outcome causes duplicate delivery/backlog | Same ID, bounded phases, consumer dedupe contract, lag metrics/recovery | Reliability gate; stop on lost event/unbounded loop |
| R-007 MEDIUM | Reactive starvation under crypto/publisher/load | Bounded isolation/concurrency and blocking detection/load test | Performance gate |
| R-008 MEDIUM | LikeC4 executable validation remains unavailable | Add/use repository-controlled approved validator before quality approval | Code/architecture quality gate; stop before final gate approval |
| R-009 MEDIUM | Unsupported Scheme rule key makes readiness unavailable | Release/migration coordination and readiness integration tests | Build/database owners |
| R-010 MEDIUM | Restore recurrence and operational alert details are absent | Document before production; verify RPO/RTO with restore evidence | Operations authority; stop before production readiness |
| R-011 HIGH | Existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` can rebuild on `main`, use direct SSH/SCP, mutable `latest`, and Geographic Reference paths | Quarantine from use; T034 replaces it; T030 verifies restricted wrapper and same digest | Build/release and deployment owners; stop publication, merge readiness, or deployment while conflict remains |
| R-012 MEDIUM | T036 validator selection may add unnecessary or vulnerable build dependencies, or validate syntax without resolving references/examples | Limit to build/test classpaths, record dependency rationale, self-test valid/invalid fixtures, execute all T003 artifacts, and independently review in T029 | Quarkus build owner/dependency gate; stop T003 on unresolved references, unvalidated examples, dependency vulnerability, or runtime-classpath leakage |
| R-013 MEDIUM | T011/T037 PostgreSQL evidence cannot execute when the local container socket is inaccessible | Preserve generated tests unchanged; rerun both suites in an authorised repository-scoped environment able to start the pinned PostgreSQL 18 image; record command and exit code | `factoryctl` execution environment; stop T012 completion/T023 on missing database evidence, but do not weaken or disable tests |
| R-014 MEDIUM | T012 construction choices could make independent black-box port testing impossible or force T037 to guess concrete internals | T012 must document a minimal stable constructor/factory and synthetic configuration seam; T037 consumes only that seam and application ports | Quarkus/test owners; stop T037 on absent construction contract or required production redesign outside T012 scope |
| R-015 HIGH | An application command, intent, use case or query view drops an approved OpenAPI/DBML fact, forcing an adapter to invent defaults or making a valid row unrepresentable | T038 field-flow tests/map, T039 bounded core repair, T011 regression rerun, T037 black-box evidence | Test/Quarkus owners; stop T012 on any missing nationality primary, identifier creation/lifecycle, verification, status or audit fact |

### Human decisions

None unresolved. A later change to business search scope, a breaking published contract, security/privacy risk acceptance, DBML, architecture, destructive operations, or production exposure still requires its designated authority; TC-001 does not grant such authority.

## 15. Pull Request and Release Handoff

The later PR must reference the issue, use the approved feature branch, summarize only planned functionality, list changed paths, include requirement/test traceability and all mandatory gate evidence, document restricted-data and no-auth residual risk, explain migration/privilege/compatibility behavior, and include rollout, reconciliation, backup/restore, application rollback, and forward-only database notes. Automerge is prohibited. Human merge confirmation is mandatory, and a human performs the GitHub merge.

After authorised merge, `build-release-agent` records source commit, reproducible build invocation, OCI digest and SBOM. Development and staging receive that exact digest. Production receives the same staging-verified digest without rebuild, only after workflow authority permits it. Environment configuration and secrets remain external. Deployment and production verification belong to later phases and agents.

## 16. Global Stop Conditions and Assumptions

Stop and return control rather than improvise on any requirement/architecture/DBML conflict, TC-001 semantic drift, public-contract incompatibility, dropped mandatory OpenAPI/DBML application field, adapter-invented placeholder/default, secret or personal-data exposure, cross-tenant access, destructive migration, Scheme runtime mutation, unbounded retry/concurrency, remote I/O inside a state-changing transaction, inaccessible mandatory PostgreSQL test environment, absent T012 construction contract, use of the existing direct-SSH/cross-service workflow, production access, missing rollback/recovery evidence, mandatory test/gate failure, unapproved dependency/version drift, or protected factory-state change.

Low-risk planning assumptions:

1. Operational numeric values not approved by requirements (publisher batch, timeout, backoff, jitter, pool limits, alert thresholds) remain bounded external configuration validated against approved targets, not new business requirements.

1: Project PartyRegistryServiceV1 {
2:   database_type: 'PostgreSQL'
3: 
4:   Note: '''
5:     Party Registry Service V1 - bounded context for tenant-scoped civil and legal identity.
6: 
7:     It is the system of record for identity data registered and maintained within
8:     each tenant. It owns Parties, their natural-person or legal-entity details,
9:     nationalities, official identifiers, and the database-managed identification
10:     scheme reference catalog used to normalize and validate those identifiers.
11: 
12:     It does not own customers, suppliers, employees, user accounts, authentication,
13:     authorization, operating organizations, addresses, contacts, subscriptions,
14:     audit storage, tax configuration, ownership structures, beneficial ownership,
15:     or legal/corporate relationship management.
16: 
17:     Other microservices keep party_id as an opaque reference and do not create
18:     foreign keys to this database.
19: 
20:     Country codes are logical references to the Geographic Reference Service,
21:     using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, without remote foreign keys.
22: 
23:     Complete identification values are encrypted with authenticated encryption.
24:     Exact lookup and permanent identifier uniqueness use a tenant-isolated
25:     HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal
26:     characters. Within one tenant and Identifier Scheme, the same normalized
27:     identifier value can never be registered more than once, regardless of
28:     lifecycle status.
29: 
30:     Identifier Schemes such as CEDULA, RUC and PASSPORT are database-managed
31:     reference data. Party Registry runtime reads them but does not create, update,
32:     delete or transition them through application use cases or REST endpoints.
33: 
34:     Keycloak authenticates accounts, but it is not the registry of persons.
35:     The relationship between an authenticated subject and party_id belongs to
36:     the Access Management Service.
37: 
38:     Every mutable business table contains created_at, created_by, updated_at and
39:     updated_by. Aggregate roots additionally contain version for optimistic
40:     concurrency control.
41: 
42:     party_outbox_events is infrastructure for reliable publication of tenant-scoped
43:     business events. It does not publish database-schema, Flyway, platform, or
44:     database-managed identifier-scheme catalog changes.

117:   version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party aggregate.']

341:   issued_on DATE
342:   expires_on DATE

361:     `(status = 'EXPIRED' AND expires_on IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'EXPIRED'` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_expired_date']
362:     `normalized_value_hash ~ '^[0-9A-F]{64}$'` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_hash_upper_hex']
363:     `normalization_version > 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_normalization_version']
364:     `encryption_key_version > 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_encryption_key_version']
365:     `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_nonnegative_version']

367: 
368:   Note: '''
369:     Aggregate for official identifiers such as national ID, RUC, passport,
370:     residence permit and legal registration number.
371: 
372:     normalized_value_hash is the canonical uppercase hexadecimal encoding of the
373:     HMAC-SHA-256 bytes. Lowercase hexadecimal, mixed case, prefixes and alternate
374:     textual encodings are invalid persisted representations.
375: 
376:     The tuple (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash) is a
377:     permanent business uniqueness key. Once a normalized identifier value has
378:     existed for a given tenant and Identifier Scheme, no second row may reuse
379:     that value, even when the previous row is REJECTED, EXPIRED or REVOKED.
380:     Lifecycle status never releases the identifier for reuse.
381: 
382:     The same normalized identifier value may exist in another tenant or under a
383:     different Identifier Scheme because either change produces a different
384:     uniqueness scope.
385: 
386:     Flyway must create the partial unique index
387:       uq_party_identifiers_verified_primary_scheme
388:     on (tenant_id, party_id, identifier_scheme_id)
389:     WHERE is_primary = true AND status = 'VERIFIED'.
390: 
391:     The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove that the
392:     permanent tenant+scheme+hash uniqueness rejects duplicate canonical hashes,
393:     the uppercase-hash check rejects lowercase/mixed/non-hex representations,
394:     and at most one VERIFIED primary identifier exists for the same
395:     tenant+Party+Identifier Scheme while non-primary or non-VERIFIED history is
396:     retained.
397: 
398:     The application must ensure that the Party type is compatible with the
399:     identifier scheme applicable_subject_type.
400: 
401:     Public integration events must never contain the complete decrypted value.
402:   '''

447:     `(status = 'FAILED' AND last_error_code IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'FAILED'` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_failed_error']

Project PartyRegistryServiceV1 {
  database_type: 'PostgreSQL'

  Note: '''
    Party Registry Service V1 - bounded context for tenant-scoped civil and legal identity.

    It is the system of record for identity data registered and maintained within
    each tenant. It owns Parties, their natural-person or legal-entity details,
    nationalities, official identifiers, and the database-managed identification
    scheme reference catalog used to normalize and validate those identifiers.

    It does not own customers, suppliers, employees, user accounts, authentication,
    authorization, operating organizations, addresses, contacts, subscriptions,
    audit storage, tax configuration, ownership structures, beneficial ownership,
    or legal/corporate relationship management.

    Other microservices keep party_id as an opaque reference and do not create
    foreign keys to this database.

    Country codes are logical references to the Geographic Reference Service,
    using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, without remote foreign keys.

    Complete identification values are encrypted with authenticated encryption.
    Exact lookup and permanent identifier uniqueness use a tenant-isolated
    HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal
    characters. Within one tenant and Identifier Scheme, the same normalized
    identifier value can never be registered more than once, regardless of
    lifecycle status.

    Identifier Schemes such as CEDULA, RUC and PASSPORT are database-managed
    reference data. Party Registry runtime reads them but does not create, update,
    delete or transition them through application use cases or REST endpoints.

    Keycloak authenticates accounts, but it is not the registry of persons.
    The relationship between an authenticated subject and party_id belongs to
    the Access Management Service.

    Every mutable business table contains created_at, created_by, updated_at and
    updated_by. Aggregate roots additionally contain version for optimistic
    concurrency control.

    party_outbox_events is infrastructure for reliable publication of tenant-scoped
    business events. It does not publish database-schema, Flyway, platform, or
    database-managed identifier-scheme catalog changes.
  '''
}

// Enums

Enum party_type {
  NATURAL_PERSON
  LEGAL_ENTITY
}

Enum party_record_status {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  INACTIVE
  ARCHIVED
}

Enum identifier_category {
  NATIONAL_ID
  TAX_ID
  PASSPORT
  RESIDENCE_PERMIT
  LEGAL_REGISTRATION_NUMBER
  OTHER
}

Enum identifier_subject_type {
  NATURAL_PERSON
  LEGAL_ENTITY
  BOTH
}

Enum identifier_scheme_status {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  DEPRECATED
  RETIRED
}

Enum party_identifier_status {
  PENDING_VERIFICATION
  VERIFIED
  REJECTED
  EXPIRED
  REVOKED
}

Enum party_outbox_aggregate_type {
  PARTY
  PARTY_IDENTIFIER
}

Enum outbox_status {
  PENDING
  PUBLISHED
  FAILED
}

// Tables

Table parties {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
  tenant_id UUID [not null, note: 'Opaque reference to the tenant that owns this Party representation.']

  type party_type [not null]
  display_name VARCHAR(300) [not null, note: 'Canonical denormalized Party display name derived by Domain/Application from the corresponding detail row and persisted atomically.']
  record_status party_record_status [not null, default: 'DRAFT']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.']
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.']
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party aggregate.']

  indexes {
    (tenant_id, id) [unique, name: 'uq_parties_tenant_id']
    (tenant_id, type, record_status) [name: 'ix_parties_tenant_type_status']
    (tenant_id, display_name) [name: 'ix_parties_tenant_display_name']
  }

  checks {
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_parties_nonnegative_version']
  }

  Note: '''
    Root of the Party aggregate. A Party is either NATURAL_PERSON or LEGAL_ENTITY.
    It is never a Customer, Supplier, Employee, User, Tenant, or operating company.

    display_name is derived deterministically by Domain/Application:
    - NATURAL_PERSON: normalize given_names and family_names independently, then
      join them with exactly one ASCII U+0020 SPACE.
    - LEGAL_ENTITY: normalize legal_name.

    Name normalization trims leading and trailing whitespace and collapses each
    internal run of whitespace to exactly one ASCII U+0020 SPACE. Letter case and
    diacritics are preserved. preferred_name and trade_name never replace the
    canonical display_name in V1. A mutation to a source name field and its
    resulting display_name update must commit atomically in the same transaction.

    Any mutation to natural_person_details, legal_entity_details or
    party_nationalities must increment parties.version in the same transaction.
  '''
}

Table natural_person_details {
  party_id UUID [pk, not null]

  given_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
  family_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
  preferred_name VARCHAR(200)
  birth_date DATE
  date_of_death DATE
  birth_country_code CHAR(2) [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  checks {
    `date_of_death IS NULL OR birth_date IS NULL OR date_of_death >= birth_date` [name: 'ck_natural_person_life_dates']
    `birth_country_code IS NULL OR birth_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_natural_person_birth_country_code']
  }

  Note: '''
    One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for NATURAL_PERSON.

    Flyway must implement one deferred party/detail integrity mechanism using
    function fn_enforce_party_detail_type and these constraint-trigger objects:
    - ct_parties_detail_type on parties for INSERT and UPDATE of type.
    - ct_natural_person_details_party_type on natural_person_details for INSERT,
      UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.
    - ct_legal_entity_details_party_type on legal_entity_details for INSERT,
      UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.

    Each constraint trigger executes AFTER the stated row event, FOR EACH ROW,
    DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, so the invariant is evaluated at transaction
    commit after Party and detail rows may have been written in either order.

    At commit, each affected Party must satisfy exactly one detail invariant:
    - NATURAL_PERSON has exactly one natural_person_details row and zero
      legal_entity_details rows.
    - LEGAL_ENTITY has exactly one legal_entity_details row and zero
      natural_person_details rows.

    The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove both valid
    insertion orderings in one transaction and must reject a missing required
    detail, a type-incompatible detail, both detail types for one Party, and any
    update/delete that would leave the committed invariant invalid.
  '''
}

Table legal_entity_details {
  party_id UUID [pk, not null]

  legal_name VARCHAR(300) [not null, note: 'Official registered name.']
  trade_name VARCHAR(300) [note: 'Primary trade name for V1; it does not replace legal_name.']
  legal_form_code VARCHAR(64) [note: 'Jurisdiction-qualified code, for example EC_SAS, EC_SA or US_LLC.']
  incorporation_country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']
  incorporated_on DATE
  dissolved_on DATE

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  checks {
    `dissolved_on IS NULL OR incorporated_on IS NULL OR dissolved_on >= incorporated_on` [name: 'ck_legal_entity_lifecycle_dates']
    `incorporation_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_legal_entity_incorporation_country_code']
  }

  Note: '''
    One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for LEGAL_ENTITY.
    It does not represent tenant configuration, tax configuration, ownership,
    corporate hierarchy, or commercial roles.
  '''
}

Table party_nationalities {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
  party_id UUID [not null]

  country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']
  is_primary BOOLEAN [not null, default: false]
  valid_from DATE
  valid_until DATE

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  indexes {
    (party_id, country_code) [name: 'ix_party_nationalities_country']
    (party_id, is_primary) [name: 'ix_party_nationalities_primary']
  }

  checks {
    `country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_party_nationality_country_code']
    `valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from IS NULL OR valid_until >= valid_from` [name: 'ck_party_nationality_validity']
  }

  Note: '''
    Nationalities known and maintained by the tenant for a natural-person Party.

    party_nationalities intentionally does not duplicate tenant_id. party_id
    references the globally unique parties.id, so the owning tenant is inherited
    unambiguously through that Party relationship.

    Flyway must create these exact partial unique indexes:
    - uq_party_nationalities_active_country on (party_id, country_code)
      WHERE valid_until IS NULL.
    - uq_party_nationalities_active_primary on (party_id)
      WHERE is_primary = true AND valid_until IS NULL.

    The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove that a Party
    cannot have two active rows for the same country, cannot have two active
    primary nationalities, may retain ended historical rows, and may create a new
    active row after the previous matching nationality has been ended.
  '''
}

Table identifier_schemes {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]

  code VARCHAR(64) [not null, unique, note: 'Global stable code, for example EC_CEDULA, EC_RUC_NATURAL or US_EIN.']
  issuing_country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'Logical ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 reference.']
  category identifier_category [not null]
  applicable_subject_type identifier_subject_type [not null]
  name VARCHAR(150) [not null]
  description VARCHAR(500)

  normalizer_key VARCHAR(64) [not null, note: 'Versioned implementation key, for example DIGITS_ONLY_V1.']
  validator_key VARCHAR(64) [not null, note: 'Versioned implementation key, for example ECUADOR_CEDULA_V1. It does not contain executable code.']
  minimum_length SMALLINT
  maximum_length SMALLINT
  requires_expiration BOOLEAN [not null, default: false]
  status identifier_scheme_status [not null, default: 'DRAFT']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0]

  indexes {
    (issuing_country_code, category, applicable_subject_type, status) [name: 'ix_identifier_schemes_country_category']
  }

  checks {
    `issuing_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_identifier_scheme_country_code']
    `minimum_length IS NULL OR minimum_length > 0` [name: 'ck_identifier_scheme_minimum_length']
    `maximum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length > 0` [name: 'ck_identifier_scheme_maximum_length']
    `minimum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length >= minimum_length` [name: 'ck_identifier_scheme_length_range']
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_identifier_schemes_nonnegative_version']
  }

  Note: '''
    Global database-managed reference catalog used internally by Party Registry
    to normalize and validate official Party identifiers, for example CEDULA,
    RUC and PASSPORT schemes.

    Party Registry runtime treats this table as read-only. The runtime database
    role must not INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE identifier_schemes rows. Scheme rows
    are introduced or changed only through the governed database migration and/or
    explicitly authorized database-administration path using separate credentials.

    Persisted status, audit and version fields describe database-managed catalog
    state; they do not imply a Party Registry REST lifecycle or Scheme
    Administration application capability.

    Database-managed Scheme changes are not published through the tenant Party
    outbox. Persisted normalizer/validator keys must remain compatible with the
    deployed Party Registry implementation catalog; the runtime fails closed on
    unusable required configuration rather than rewriting this table.
  '''
}

Table party_identifiers {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
  tenant_id UUID [not null]
  party_id UUID [not null]
  identifier_scheme_id UUID [not null]

  issuer_code VARCHAR(64) [note: 'Issuing authority, for example SRI or REGISTRO_CIVIL.']

  encrypted_value TEXT [not null, note: 'Authenticated encryption; never plain text.']
  encryption_key_version SMALLINT [not null, note: 'Version of the runtime-injected encryption key used for this ciphertext.']
  normalized_value_hash CHAR(64) [not null, note: 'Tenant-isolated HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal characters; used for exact lookup and permanent uniqueness within the tenant and Identifier Scheme.']
  masked_value VARCHAR(64) [not null, note: 'Safe representation for UI and logs.']
  normalization_version SMALLINT [not null, default: 1]

  is_primary BOOLEAN [not null, default: false, note: 'Primary identifier within the same Party and identifier scheme.']
  status party_identifier_status [not null, default: 'PENDING_VERIFICATION']

  issued_on DATE
  expires_on DATE
  verified_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  verified_by VARCHAR(128)

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party Identifier aggregate.']

  indexes {
    (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash) [unique, name: 'uq_party_identifier_tenant_scheme_hash']
    (tenant_id, party_id, identifier_scheme_id, status) [name: 'ix_party_identifiers_party_scheme_status']
    (tenant_id, party_id, is_primary) [name: 'ix_party_identifiers_primary']
  }

  checks {
    `expires_on IS NULL OR issued_on IS NULL OR expires_on >= issued_on` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_validity_dates']
    `(status = 'VERIFIED' AND verified_at IS NOT NULL AND verified_by IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'VERIFIED'` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_verification']
    `(status = 'EXPIRED' AND expires_on IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'EXPIRED'` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_expired_date']
    `normalized_value_hash ~ '^[0-9A-F]{64}$'` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_hash_upper_hex']
    `normalization_version > 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_normalization_version']
    `encryption_key_version > 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_encryption_key_version']
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_nonnegative_version']
  }

  Note: '''
    Aggregate for official identifiers such as national ID, RUC, passport,
    residence permit and legal registration number.

    normalized_value_hash is the canonical uppercase hexadecimal encoding of the
    HMAC-SHA-256 bytes. Lowercase hexadecimal, mixed case, prefixes and alternate
    textual encodings are invalid persisted representations.

    The tuple (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash) is a
    permanent business uniqueness key. Once a normalized identifier value has
    existed for a given tenant and Identifier Scheme, no second row may reuse
    that value, even when the previous row is REJECTED, EXPIRED or REVOKED.
    Lifecycle status never releases the identifier for reuse.

    The same normalized identifier value may exist in another tenant or under a
    different Identifier Scheme because either change produces a different
    uniqueness scope.

    Flyway must create the partial unique index
      uq_party_identifiers_verified_primary_scheme
    on (tenant_id, party_id, identifier_scheme_id)
    WHERE is_primary = true AND status = 'VERIFIED'.

    The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove that the
    permanent tenant+scheme+hash uniqueness rejects duplicate canonical hashes,
    the uppercase-hash check rejects lowercase/mixed/non-hex representations,
    and at most one VERIFIED primary identifier exists for the same
    tenant+Party+Identifier Scheme while non-primary or non-VERIFIED history is
    retained.

    The application must ensure that the Party type is compatible with the
    identifier scheme applicable_subject_type.

    Public integration events must never contain the complete decrypted value.
  '''
}

Table party_outbox_events {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`, note: 'Integration event identifier.']
  tenant_id UUID [not null]

  aggregate_type party_outbox_aggregate_type [not null]
  aggregate_id UUID [not null]
  aggregate_version BIGINT [not null]

  event_type VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Versioned business contract, for example party.created.v1 or party.identifier-verified.v1.']
  event_schema_version SMALLINT [not null, default: 1]
  payload JSONB [not null, note: 'Minimal integration payload without full identifiers or unnecessary personal data.']

  occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  correlation_id VARCHAR(128)
  causation_id VARCHAR(128)

  status outbox_status [not null, default: 'PENDING']
  publish_attempts INTEGER [not null, default: 0]
  next_attempt_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  last_attempt_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  published_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  last_error_code VARCHAR(64)
  last_error_detail VARCHAR(1000)

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Service principal that created the business event.']
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Publisher instance or service principal that last changed delivery state.']
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version for delivery-state transitions.']

  indexes {
    (status, next_attempt_at, created_at) [name: 'ix_party_outbox_delivery']
    (tenant_id, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, aggregate_version) [name: 'ix_party_outbox_aggregate']
    correlation_id [name: 'ix_party_outbox_correlation']
  }

  checks {
    `aggregate_version >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_aggregate_version']
    `event_schema_version > 0` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_positive_schema_version']
    `publish_attempts >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_attempts']
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_version']
    `(status = 'PUBLISHED' AND published_at IS NOT NULL) OR (status <> 'PUBLISHED' AND published_at IS NULL)` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_published_at']
    `(status = 'FAILED' AND last_error_code IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'FAILED'` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_failed_error']
  }

  Note: '''
    Transactional Outbox for tenant-scoped Party Registry business events.

    The business mutation and outbox insertion must be committed in the same
    PostgreSQL transaction. A separate publisher processes PENDING rows using
    SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

    Aggregate mapping:
    - PARTY: aggregate_id = parties.id and aggregate_version = parties.version.
      This includes changes to natural_person_details, legal_entity_details and
      party_nationalities; parties.version must be incremented in the same transaction.
    - PARTY_IDENTIFIER: aggregate_id = party_identifiers.id and
      aggregate_version = party_identifiers.version.

    The table does not publish:
    - PostgreSQL schema changes.
    - Flyway migrations.
    - Platform or infrastructure events.
    - database-managed identifier_schemes catalog changes.

    Delivery is at-least-once. Consumers must be idempotent using id as event_id.
  '''
}

// References

Ref: natural_person_details.(party_id) - parties.(id) [delete: restrict]

Ref: legal_entity_details.(party_id) - parties.(id) [delete: restrict]

Ref: party_nationalities.(party_id) > parties.(id) [delete: restrict]

Ref: party_identifiers.(tenant_id, party_id) > parties.(tenant_id, id) [delete: restrict]

Ref: party_identifiers.identifier_scheme_id > identifier_schemes.id [delete: restrict]
